description: Known FiberHMM changes that alter results, and how to tell whether an output was made before them. Read by fiberhmm.advisories / fiberhmm-check. The advisories list is maintained by hand; tables, commits and commits_through are regenerated by tools/build_advisory_index.py.

severities.rerun-required: The output was made by code or tables with a known error; re-run it.
severities.rerun-recommended: The output was made under rules that 3.0 corrects; re-run it where those rules matter.
severities.unverifiable: The output carries FiberHMM results but records no FiberHMM provenance, so it cannot be checked; re-run it if it came from FiberHMM < 3.0 (or you cannot tell).
severities.info: A default changed; the output is not wrong, but a 3.0 run with defaults would differ.

advisories.title: Nanopore Hia5 calls made with the context-swapped emission table
advisories.reason: The Nanopore Hia5 emission table shipped in every 2.x release was indexed in ACGT context order while the encoder uses A, C, T, G, so every context containing G or T read another context's emission. Nucleosome, MSP and TF calls all used it. With the fixed table about 75-83% of calls keep both edges within 5 bp; call totals are about unchanged.
advisories.fix: Re-call from the aligned reads with FiberHMM >= 3.0: fiberhmm-call -i aligned.bam -o calls.bam --enzyme hia5 --seq nanopore (or fiberhmm-pipeline). fiberhmm-recall-tfs alone is not enough: the footprint pass used the same table. Re-run QC and consensus made from the old calls.

advisories.title: DddB calls made with the context-swapped emission table
advisories.reason: The bundled DddB emission table was indexed in ACGT context order while the encoder uses A, C, T, G (the same error as the Nanopore Hia5 table), so contexts containing G or T read another context's emission in footprint and recall passes.
advisories.fix: Re-call from the aligned reads with FiberHMM >= 3.0: fiberhmm-call -i aligned.bam -o calls.bam --enzyme dddb (or fiberhmm-pipeline). Re-run QC and consensus made from the old calls.

advisories.title: Nanopore Hia5 reads called as PacBio
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 a Hia5 run without --seq assumed PacBio, so Nanopore reads were called with the PacBio table and observation frame (not strand-aware). 3.0 detects the platform from the input's chemistry declaration, MM tags and header.
advisories.fix: Re-call from the aligned reads with FiberHMM >= 3.0: fiberhmm-call -i aligned.bam -o calls.bam --enzyme hia5 --seq nanopore (or fiberhmm-pipeline).

advisories.title: Custom table on DddA/DddB input run without the enzyme's defaults
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 a custom -m/--model without --enzyme on a DddA- or DddB-called BAM did not inherit that enzyme's defaults (CC/GG keep-one run mask, CpG masking, ML threshold, TF presets, nucleosome model), so the run differed from --enzyme <enzyme> with the same table.
advisories.fix: Re-run the same command with FiberHMM >= 3.0 (the table then inherits the input's enzyme defaults), or pass --enzyme ddda/dddb together with -m.
advisories.changelog: 3.0.0 / Fixed / Calling entry points; fiberhmm-apply chemistry

advisories.title: DAF duplicates grouped by alignment orientation
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 DAF dedup grouped reads by alignment orientation instead of deamination flavour (C->T vs G->A), so PCR copies aligned in opposite orientations were not marked (e.g. about 5.8% -> 9.9% duplicates on one DddA dataset). MM/ML dU input was also read at ML >= 0 instead of 128.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-dedup (or fiberhmm-call --dedup) on the un-deduplicated input with FiberHMM >= 3.0, then re-run what was made from it (pairing, calls, QC).
advisories.changelog: 3.0.0 / Changed defaults / Duplicates by deamination flavour

advisories.title: fiberhmm-pair paired reads flagged as PCR duplicates
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 fiberhmm-pair used 0x400-flagged PCR duplicates as pairing candidates, so a duplicate could take a molecule's partner and its merged consensus. Only inputs that carried duplicate flags (fiberhmm-dedup --flag-only, or fiberhmm-call's marking) are affected.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-pair (pair -> merge -> recall) on the duplicate-flagged input with FiberHMM >= 3.0.

advisories.title: fiberhmm-tag-m5c wrote no unmethylated-island (ddda_ucg) spans
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 fiberhmm-tag-m5c did not write unmethylated whole-island calls as ddda_ucg, so fiberhmm-recall-tfs --use-m5c masked every CpG instead of exempting confident unmethylated islands.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-tag-m5c with FiberHMM >= 3.0, then fiberhmm-recall-tfs --use-m5c.

advisories.title: Posteriors decoded reverse reads in the wrong frame
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 fiberhmm-posteriors decoded reverse-strand reads outside the call's frame, did not handle DAF, and did not resolve --seq and the ML threshold like fiberhmm-call (Hia5 Nanopore 248).

advisories.title: Nanopore QC counted the wrong strand's A's and '?' bases
advisories.reason: Before 3.0 fiberhmm-qc counted, for Nanopore Hia5 reads aligned to the reverse strand, the opposite strand's A's as opportunities, and counted bases an MM '?' entry leaves unlisted as unmodified. Per-read rates shift by about +/-1-2% at the quartiles ('?' data more). PacBio, R/Y and MD QC is unchanged.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-qc on the BAM with FiberHMM >= 3.0.

advisories.title: QC report graded under a misdetected assay
advisories.reason: Standalone fiberhmm-qc (and so fiberhmm-pipeline) took the assay mode from the first 'mode=' anywhere in the BAM header. On a deduplicated DAF BAM that is fiberhmm-dedup's mode=flag (or mode=collapse), so the sample was graded without the DAF metrics or reference (typically INSUFFICIENT with 0% labelling). The QC fiberhmm-call runs itself was not affected.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-qc giving the assay explicitly (--mode daf --enzyme ddda/dddb, or --mode pacbio-fiber/nanopore-fiber); with FiberHMM 3.0.0, whose fiberhmm-qc reads the assay from the chemistry declaration, the defaults also work.

advisories.title: Lattice-recaller edge/loose prevalence tiers double-counted molecules
advisories.reason: Before the 3.0 fix the looser prevalence tiers added a member's probability again instead of only a non-member's remaining 1 - P, so edge and loose tiers were too high (by up to 0.137, typically 0.002-0.04) and could exceed 1. Core prevalence is unchanged.
advisories.fix: Re-run fiberhmm-consensus with FiberHMM >= 3.0 on the same BAMs and parameters.

advisories.title: Nanopore Hia5 called at the old default ML threshold
advisories.reason: 3.0 calls Hia5 Nanopore m6A at ML >= 248 by default (2.x: 128). This run did not set --prob-threshold, so it used the old default.
advisories.fix: Nothing is wrong. To match 3.0 defaults re-call with FiberHMM >= 3.0; pass --prob-threshold 128 to reproduce the old threshold.
advisories.changelog: 3.0.0 / Changed defaults / ML threshold per chemistry

advisories.title: Secondary and supplementary alignments were called
advisories.reason: 3.0 fiberhmm-call and fiberhmm-apply call primary alignments only by default (secondary/supplementary records pass through uncalled). This run did not choose, so it called every alignment.
advisories.fix: Nothing is wrong. To match 3.0 defaults re-call with FiberHMM >= 3.0; --no-primary keeps the old behaviour.

advisories.title: DddA recall used CpG observations
advisories.reason: 3.0 excludes CpG observations from DddA nucleosome and TF recall in fiberhmm-call and the joint recall of fiberhmm-pair/-merge (except inside confident unmethylated islands, ddda_ucg), as fiberhmm-recall-tfs does. This run predates that default.
advisories.fix: Nothing is wrong. To match 3.0 defaults re-call with FiberHMM >= 3.0; --no-use-m5c keeps CpG observations.
advisories.changelog: 3.0.0 / Changed defaults / DddA CpG-aware recall everywhere

advisories.title: Footprint calls without FiberHMM provenance (cannot verify)
advisories.reason: Reads carry footprint calls but the header has no fiberhmm-call/-apply/-recall @PG record (fiberhmm-apply and fiberhmm-recall-tfs wrote none before 3.0, and 2.x releases before 2.13 wrote none at all; the header may also have been replaced). Which version and tables made the calls cannot be checked, so no fix can be ruled out: calls made by FiberHMM before 3.0 may carry errors 3.0 corrects (for example the context-swapped 2.x Nanopore Hia5 and DddB tables).
advisories.fix: If the calls came from FiberHMM < 3.0, or you cannot tell, re-call from the aligned reads with FiberHMM >= 3.0 (its header records the version and tables); otherwise check how the file was made.
